title: Five Images, Six Decades: Capturing the Iconic “Earthrise” Photo - Nautilus
gist: NASA's Lunar Orbiter 1 captured the first 'Earthrise' image—Earth rising above the lunar surface—on August 23, 1966, sixty years before this piece.

insights.claim: NASA's Lunar Orbiter 1 captured the first-ever 'Earthrise' image, showing Earth rising above the lunar surface, on August 23, 1966.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Anchors the historical origin of one of spaceflight's most iconic images.
insights.locator: On August 23, 1966, NASA’s first lunar orbiter snapped the header photo

insights.claim: Lunar Orbiter 1 launched from Cape Canaveral on August 10, 1966, took a few hundred more lunar images over a year, then met its end by diving into the lunar surface.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Documents the short operational lifespan of an early lunar imaging mission.
insights.locator: a few weeks after it launched from Cape Canaveral
